⭐ the fixed engine->track-file entry, called once from engine_init. It arrives WITH the track data (the unpack swap deposits the track file over $5300-$5A25), so it is not a patch site. SILVER: 60 EA EA = RTS/NOP/NOP, a deliberate no-op for the circuit with no hook code. BRANDS: 4C 00 57 = JMP $5700. One call, one target — a far cleaner seam for the port than the five patch sites. ⭐⭐ IN THIS PORT IT IS CORRECTLY A NO-OP FOR EVERY CIRCUIT, and that is not the same as baking Silverstone's RTS by accident: on an expansion circuit $5A22 holds JMP $5700 = ModifyGameCode, whose whole job is to patch the engine, and the port applies that patcher's OUTPUT as data at selection time (tools/track_patch.py replays it; `make track-patch VERIFY=1` cross-checks the replay against a real BBC). Running it here would patch an already-patched image. The guarantee that the replay covered whatever is there is a GENERATION-time one: the replay's interpreter raises on any opcode outside its twelve-form vocabulary. src/platform/track.h, docs/phases.md §5.

the ONLY routine that programs the hardware: 6845 CRTC ($FE00/$FE01), Video ULA palette ($FE21), System VIA T1/ACR/IFR/IER, User VIA T1/ACR/IER. 54 instructions, one caller. This is the platform boundary.

⭐ THE RASTER-BAND PALETTE/MODE SCHEDULE, claimed via IRQ1V — and it DRAWS NOTHING (measured 2026-08-17; it was called 'the 50 Hz game body' until then, and that misnomer is why the row was carried as untouchable engine work). Driven by a USER VIA T1 timeout (LDA $FE6D / AND #$40), NOT System VIA vsync. One PAL field is five interrupts; each arm repaints the ULA mode + palette for the band about to be scanned and reloads the T1 latch with that band's duration — the raster split a BBC has to do on the CPU for want of a copper. Dispatches on irq_band_state; chains to saved_irq1v when the interrupt is not its own. The only game work in the whole cycle is the JSR tick_wheel_spin ($52A4) in band 4: 206-233 us of a 6113 us field, i.e. 4%.

The six addresses are three SYMMETRIC LEFT/RIGHT PAIRS in frame-buffer terms ($5A80 + row*320 + cell*8 + line): ($6E85,$6FBD) = cells 0 and 39, lines 133-135; ($6E8A,$6FB2) = cells 1 and 38, lines 133-134; ($6FC0,$70F8) = cells 0 and 39, lines 136-140. ⭐⭐ [DERIVED] THE 3D VIEWPORT RASTERISER — the biggest main-loop item in the port (30.5% / 131 ms, docs/perf-method.md). It paints ONE SCAN LINE PER CHAIN, top down: $70/$71 = $6700 and $72/$73 = $6800, and $6700 - BBC_SCREEN_BASE ($5A80) = 3200 = 10*320 exactly, i.e. character row 10 / cell 0 / line 0 = DISPLAY LINE 80, while $6800 = $6700+256 is cell 32 of the same row. So the 40 chain units are the 40 CELLS ACROSS a line (unit i writes base + 8*i, and cells 32-39 come off the second pointer because 40*8 = 320 > 256), and X = $4F..$03 is the line, stepped by $7EF3 (+1 within a character row, +$139 across one). Confirmed independently on a real BBC: stores cover display lines 80..157, buckets 88..111 full at 320 = 8 lines x 40 cells (`make fbwrites`). Each unit is `LDY srcTable,X / BEQ / LDA #0 / STA srcTable,X / LDA $6000,Y / LDY #cell*8 / STA (zp),Y` over the $80-spaced source blocks $3000..$4380 — one block per CELL COLUMN, indexed by line — and A carries left to right, so a zero source means 'same byte as the cell to my LEFT'. THREE phases by how much of the line is painted: phase 1 ($7BE2, X=$4F..$2C) all 40 cells; phases 2 ($7D13, X=$2B..$1C) and 3 ($7F18, X=$1B..$03) plant an RTS to stop the chain at a per-line cell and compose the boundary byte themselves — the silhouette of the cockpit opening. Measured: 2093 units run per sweep for ~83 changed bytes (docs/direct-bitplane-plan.md §7a). Self-modifying by construction — 42 patch sites, docs/static-map.md §Open items 10.

view_paint_lines phase 2 (X=$2B..$1C): plants the chain-A stop RTS from $3150,X and the chain-B start from $30D0,X, runs the chain, then composes the two boundary bytes itself. Reached only by falling out of $7BE2.

view_paint_lines phase 3 (X=$1B..$03): as phase 2 but plants BOTH chains' stop cells ($3150,X and $3080,X) and both start offsets, and steps the scan-line pointers itself instead of via $7EF3. Reached only from $7D13; exits through view_paint_restore.

view_paint_lines' exit: puts `STA` ($91) back over the three RTS opcodes the sweep planted (the slots recorded in $7D24/$7F24/$7F7D) and `CPX` ($E0) back at $7EEE, leaving the chain unpatched for the next call.

The per-frame body is $1701-$1748 — 24 top-level JSRs, PROBE bracket 1..24 — followed by the tail $174B-$17B7: INC $4F43 while negative, the field_countdown delay on the $62F6 path ($175B, spun on at $1760), shift_key_commands with Y=$0B, engine_sound_update and draw_dash_needles, then JMP $1701. It EXITS at $17BA (copy_dash_data with A=$80, stowing the overlay back into the block tails, then $4F23) and RTSes: it is JSRed from wait_flag_05F4 ($6563), so control returns to the front end. In the port $1701 is the frame/paint hook and $1760 the frame-wait spin; the front end never reaches either (docs/phases.md). TWIN #3 (src/gen/revs_native.c): a native DRIVER — the three restart targets are a nested RestartDepth, the tail is a LoopVerdict, and both port hooks are spelled out by hand because the transpiler emits them only into the oracle. It is in NATIVE_FUNCS, not VALIDATE_FUNCS: no fixture can exist for it, and make determinism + make determinism-drive are the gate.

⭐ THE IN-RACE COMMAND KEYS, called once per frame from race_main_loop's tail ($1791) with Y=$0B. Returns immediately unless SHIFT (negative INKEY -1, X=$FF) is held; then scans shift_key_tbl[Y..0] and applies that key's shift_key_action_tbl byte to state_flags+index. The second half services two of the cells it just wrote: pause_request negative = stop all sound and spin in clear_surface_buffers until key $A6 is pressed (a real PAUSE), positive = INC engine_note; volume_change_request steps sound_volume by one, positive louder (DEY, floor $F1 = -15) and negative quieter (INY, ceiling 0), then writes amplitude*8 into envelope_attack_level and redefines envelope 1. Both arms INC engine_note so the note is nudged on resume.

(a) steps time_tick_countdown down, reloading it from time_tick_period+1 at zero; (b) unless start_light_state is negative, adds one frame to the player's clock through add_frame_time with X=0 — so the race clock does NOT run until the starting lights have gone out; (c) INCs loop_counter and carries into loop_counter_hi; (d) every 32nd frame (loop_counter AND $1F), and only once race_clock_mid[0] is non-zero, calls $635D to refresh the non-player drivers' speeds. Also called once per iteration by finish_race.

⭐ [DERIVED] adds ONE FRAME of elapsed time to driver X's 3-byte clock, in BCD (it runs under SED). +$09 into race_clock_lo, or +$18 on the single frame where time_tick_countdown equals time_tick_period, then the carry into race_clock_mid (wrapped at BCD 60) and race_clock_hi. ⭐ With time_tick_period = $18 that averages 9.36 hundredths of a second per main-loop frame — i.e. the clock is calibrated to the BBC's own ~10.7 frames a second, and the $18 frame is the correction that makes the average exact. A negative race_clock_hi means the clock overflowed: clear_race_clock resets it and $04DC[player_car] is flagged $80.
[DERIVED] counts down time_tick_period+1 .. 0 and reloads, stepped by tick_race_timers. add_frame_time adds its corrected $18 on the one frame it equals time_tick_period.

[DERIVED] the reload for time_tick_countdown ($18 = 24 for Silverstone, so a 25-frame cycle) and the value add_frame_time compares against. In the per-circuit track block ($5300-$5A39, the half of the $5300<->$70DB swap), so each circuit carries its own.

[DERIVED] the main loop's frame counter, INCed once per frame by tick_race_timers; loop_counter_hi is its high byte. The `AND #$1F` on it is what makes the driver-speed refresh every 32nd frame, and draw_starting_lights' `AND #$3F` is what holds each light for 64 frames.
high byte of loop_counter. finish_race stops at $0E out of a race.

[DERIVED] the body's 2nd call, and it lives in the $7B00 overlay (disasm/dashcode.txt, `make dashcode`). Returns at once unless session_is_race is negative. Walks start_light_state through its sequence ($80 -> $A0 -> ... -> 0, with the $A0 arm waiting on loop_counter AND $3F and the $80 arm forcing $F0 while the engine is not running) and paints the light column STRAIGHT INTO view_src_blocks column 37 — $F0 into $42C0-$42C9, then the state's pattern into $42C2-$42C7 EORed with a second value. Column 37 is the screen's right edge.

[DERIVED] the starting-light sequence's state, NEGATIVE while the lights are still showing: tick_race_timers refuses to advance the race clock until it is positive, draw_starting_lights walks it, and finish_race zeroes it.

⭐ [DERIVED] the body's 3rd call — THE DRIVING CONTROLS, all of them. It spans $1579-$16DB; the listing splits it at $15F4 and $1612 only because $1EE9/$1EFA/$1F9B jump back into the middle of it. (a) STEERING: joystick ($05F5 negative) reads adc_read channel 1, keyboard reads keys $A9/$A8 into a demand in $76; either way the demand passes through $1EE9/$1EFA — the assisted-steering path, which reads the track edges at $5E40/$5E90 and the assist level via $63C5 — and arrives at $1612, which subtracts the delta from steer_angle_hi/lo, wraps at $C8, clamps the magnitude to $91 and stores it. (b) THROTTLE/BRAKE: from $163B, gated on session_end_countdown; joystick channel 2 or keys $AE/$BE, into $3E/$3F. (c) GEARS: keys $9F/$EF step gear_index by +-1 at $16C5 (wrapping $FF to 0 and 7 to 6) and call draw_gear_indicator.

⭐ [DERIVED] THE STEERING ANGLE, low byte — element 2 of car_angle_lo. ⚠ Bit 0 is the SIGN and bit 7 the value's own lowest bit: every writer stores it as `ASL / ROL` of a 16-bit quantity ($0D3F, $1612), and $1F1C-$1F29 recovers the signed pair with `LSR / BCC / negate`. Written only by read_driving_controls' $1612 arm, which clamps the magnitude to $91; read by draw_dash_needles for the steering-wheel mark, by the assisted-steering path ($1F19-$1FA4), and by $4885 as part of the array. ⭐ It is the WHEEL's position and not a heading relative to the road — the alternative reading docs/rename.md item 2 raised: the only writer is the control read, and every $1Fxx reader of it is inside that same control path, not the view pipeline.
high byte of steer_angle_lo — element 2 of car_angle_hi, and the byte the $91 clamp applies to.

[DERIVED] three 16-bit angles, low bytes — bit 0 is the sign and bit 7 the value's lowest bit; the high bytes are car_angle_hi, so element i is ($62A0+i, $62A3+i). $0D01, called only from apply_driving_model, computes elements 0 and 1 and ORs their sign bits into $62A0/$62A1; element 2 is steer_angle_lo. $4880-$4888 reads a pair back by index.
the three high bytes; see car_angle_lo.

⭐ [DERIVED] the body's 4th call — the player car's PHYSICS, and nothing else in the loop writes the car's motion. A flat sequence of sub-models ($0D01 for the two car angles, then $48B9, $4729, $4BCF, $49CE, $4779, $47A5, $4779 again, $47C5, $47F9, $4C65, $48C1, $4937, $48EF, $44EA) around a 16-bit accumulator in $62D8/$62E8 that $3A/$3B is added into. It is where road_speed ($46C0) and wheel_spin_rate ($46CD) get their values, and it zeroes $62D5,X/$62E5,X for X=2..0 once $2D reaches 2.

[DERIVED] the body's 6th call — where the player sits WITHIN the current track section. Takes the section direction ($5E) minus the car's heading ($44) through $3450, folds it into one quadrant, scales it by the section distance $10 (via $4676, a piecewise table lookup times $10) and writes the two per-driver cells the rest of the engine compares between cars: $0178,X (compared at $271E-$2762, stepped by the other-car AI at $28A5-$28DF, and read by $11AB when a car is spun out) and $0164,X (differenced at $27A4, accumulated at $2887). X is player_car; $1FA8 records a change of $16 or more into $62FB. [INFERRED] which of the two is 'along' the section and which is 'across' it.

[DERIVED] the body's 7th call — moves the player BETWEEN track sections. Compares the car's heading $44 against $62E2 and, on the size of the difference and the subdivision count $13 that build_track_geometry left, calls $12F3 (step the section cursor $24 forward by 3, mod $78 = 40 sections x 3 bytes, keeping the previous value in $23), $140B (step it back, twice) or $13FB. What moves is the cursor into the $0900/$0A00 section arrays, not the car.

[DERIVED] the body's 8th call — the session's clocks and the messages along the top of the screen. RACE arm (session_is_race negative): on the $66 flag it prints the gap through $65C8/$37D0 and, once, a message via print_message_pair with token $35; then calls $1B84 unless session_end_countdown is already running. PRACTICE/QUALIFYING arm: adds a frame to clock 1 through add_frame_time — the LAP timer, separate from the player's race clock — runs the $62EF countdown behind the lap-time display ($501D/$502D/$502F/$3D50), and at $106F compares qualify_minutes against race_clock_hi[0]: equal prints token $29 once (flagging $65 bit 6), and once the elapsed minutes pass it, $65 goes $C0, session_end_countdown is armed with $3C = 60 frames and token $2A is printed.

⭐ [DERIVED] the body's 11th call — the ROAD RASTERISER, the consumer of build_track_geometry's edge lists and the producer view_paint_lines consumes, 21% of the port's frame. Seeds plot_ptr_lo with $80, then runs $193E/$19AF four times over the two edge lists with the fill selector $32 stepping $00 -> $08 -> $10 -> $1C and $8C selecting the surface, over ranges taken from horizon_index clamped up to $31 (as +$28) and to $09; the two span limits come back in $2C and $29. Writes view_src_blocks only — no screen store of its own.

[DERIVED] the body's 14th call — assembles the road sign into OBJECT SLOT $17 (23), which the body's 15th call then draws. Takes the sign from the player's section ($06E8,X) through the high nibble of the $5300 track block, remembers the last one in $62F9, reads its three coordinates from $53D0/$53E0/$53F0 and its size and type from $59EA,X (per-circuit track data), projects them ($1208, $2147, $2AB3, $2287, $2A76) and leaves the result in the object arrays, writing $008A/$008B into $0397/$03AF.

[DERIVED] the body's 15th call, entered with X = the OBJECT SLOT ($17 from the main loop). Returns at once when $018C,X is negative (an empty slot). Otherwise: size from the low nibble into $37, the object's position ($0380,X/$0398,X) minus the player's ($0A/$0B), reject anything outside $E0..$20, screen row $35 = 4*delta + $50, column from $03B0,X and width from $03C8,X, then the object plotter $1FB4. Slots hold both cars and signs, which is why the main loop reuses it for the sign it has just built. Exits with X reloaded from $45.

[DERIVED] the body's 16th call — draws the up-to-three corner markers build_track_geometry collected, then ZEROES marker_count, so the list is per-frame. Per marker: marker_flags bit 5 patches surface_colours+2 ($38FE) to $0F for the draw and back to $F0 after (⚠ an undeclared self-modifying site — docs/static-map.md), the 16-bit marker_offset is added to the edge point at $5E40/$5E90[marker_edge_index], anything landing outside $18..$E8 is skipped, and the rest becomes a row ($35 = 4*y + $50), a column (edge_y[marker_edge_index]), a width ($2A, absolute) and $37 = 6 for the object plotter $1FB4.
[DERIVED] how many corner markers this frame has, 0-3. $25D9-$25FB appends and INCs it while build_track_geometry walks the track ahead; draw_corner_markers consumes and zeroes it.
3 entries: which edge-list point each corner marker hangs off — the edge_cursor value at the moment it was appended.
3 entries: the marker's flag byte, from the track section byte ANDed with $306C,Y. Bit 5 switches its colour (draw_corner_markers' $38FE patch), bit 0 halves its offset.
3 entries: the marker's 16-bit offset from its edge point, low byte.
3 entries: high byte of marker_offset_lo.

[DERIVED] the body's 17th call — the OTHER CARS. Returns immediately when qualify_minutes is negative, i.e. during practice, where there are none. Clears bit 7 of the car-ahead's object slot, runs the motion passes $27ED, $2692, $261F and $63A2, then draws at MOST FIVE: Y counts 5 down to 0 while $5084/$507E (chosen on the $25 direction bit) walk to the next visible car for $28F2, with the working index parked in $001D/$62F4 across the calls. Finishes with $66DF and one more $28F2 for the car ahead.

[DERIVED] the body's 18th call — makes the view meet the tyres and the dashboard without a seam. Two passes of $1DEF: columns 3-6 with plot_ptr2 at $0504, and columns $1A-$22 with it at $4400. For each column $1DA6 walks the block from its dash_block_starts offset up to offset $7F and replaces every ZERO source byte with the colour column_surface_colour ($1E9E) returns; with its store operand patched to plot_ptr2 it fills view_left_start_src / view_right_start_src instead — so this call is the PRODUCER of the two per-line boundary source bytes view_paint_lines composes the runs' edge cells from.

[DERIVED] the body's 21st call — moves the raster band split with the hills, and that is the whole of 'moving the horizon'. Takes $3C - horizon_extent, clamps it to $F5..$12, halves it twice keeping the sign, then adds $D8 + $0400 and writes the 16-bit result into band1_duration_lo/hi under SEI/CLI, because irq1v_band_schedule reads it from interrupt context. It touches nothing else.

[DERIVED] the body's 22nd call — the frame's car-to-car CONTACT, gated on the $68 flag, which it clears. Scales the impact as ($25 - $41, floored at 5) * 2; at $28 or more during a race it calls $11AB to spin the struck car out, and it credits $0B to the loser's $0150 entry. The closing rate goes through mul8, is clamped to $10, and lands in $62E2. Then $80 into $62A6 AND $62A7 — the two cells engine_sound_update's first eight instructions read to pick a skid noise — and sound 4 is queued.

[DERIVED] the body's 23rd call — did the car hit the fence? Does nothing while $11 is under 2. Otherwise $5E goes through $3450: under $60 it is a scrape and it joins process_car_contact's tail at $1C0B (skid cells, sound 4). At $60 or more it is a CRASH: DEC crash_flag 0 -> $FF (the flag race_main_loop's tail reads for exactly one frame), INC horizon_extent, $3D5C and $43F6 to show the fence, sound 4, then zero $62D0-$62EE, engine_running, engine_note, engine_note_target and $26, and set $2D to $7F and $09 to $1F.

Zeroes $00-$68 and $6280-$62FF, redefines sound envelope 1, then rebuilds the per-slot arrays: for all 24 object slots the sign source from $59FE/$59FF into $08D0/$08E8 and zeroes into $06E8/$0880, and for the 20 drivers $80 into $018C/$04DC, $FF into $01A4, zeroes into $04B4/$0114/$0164/$0150/$0100/$3850. Sets gear_index and $30 to 1, $09 to 7, $06/$08 to 6, $6293-$6295 to 1, and draws the gear indicator. Ends with the session's opening message: practice/qualifying prints token $28 through print_message_pair, clears clock 1 and seeds $62EF with $DF; the race arm sets $66/$62FE, prints tokens $2B/$2C and seeds pass_count_bcd.

[DERIVED] the shallowest restart step, RESTART_LATE — rebuilds the player's car in the world. With X = player_car and Y = the current section $22 it calls $2937 to place the car, copies the three coordinate bytes from $09FD/$0AFD into $6280/$6283, advances the section by 3 (mod $78) and calls $2937 again, then loads the player's own position into $0A/$0B (the high byte EORed with the direction flag $25) — the origin every projection in the frame subtracts.

[DERIVED] the last step of every (re)start: turns the two wing settings the pit-lane menu left in $5F3D/$5F3E into the numbers the driving model uses. Per wing i: ($5F3D+i)*4 in $75 times $0BA0+i, plus $5A, into $62A8+i. Then (3*$5F3E + $5F3D)/2 + $3C into $62F1.

[DERIVED] prints message X on one status row and the fixed message $2D on another — $4D70 and $4D74 are the same printer differing only in the cursor value they store into $62CD ($21 vs $18). Every caller wants both lines: reset_driving_variables (token $28), update_lap_timers (token $35) and race_main_loop's session end (token $30).

[DERIVED] called once when a session really ends, so the results table is real: it races the REMAINING drivers to the finish with the player parked. Zeroes wheel_spin_rate and start_light_state, then loops over tick_race_timers, shift_key_commands (so the player can still abort) and the other-car passes $27ED/$2692/$63A2 until every one of the 20 drivers has either finished ($018C,X bit 6) or fallen behind $6E laps — or, outside a race, until loop_counter_hi reaches $0E. It draws nothing, which is why the screen holds the last painted frame while it runs.
